description: Every headline claim the project makes, mapped to the committed artefact that backs it, the test that asserts it against the shipped path, and the single command a stranger runs to verify it — without trusting the maintainer. tests/test_claims_ledger.py turns this into a build gate: each artefact + asserting test + one-command target must exist, and the human-track items (which code cannot produce) must stay marked not-built. This is the machine-readable form of the sprint's integrity spine.

buildableClaims.claim: The reference MCP server passes the published CACP v0.1 conformance suite (14/14 across L1 catalogue, L2 referral lifecycle, L3 consent+audit).
escolib resolves occupational synonyms to canonical ESCO/ISCO codes standalone (no application import), with a 100%-recall / 0-false-positive benchmark on committed fixtures.
biasprobe replays the committed model-response caches into a comparative per-persona bias report offline, with zero application import.
The audit chain is anchorable to a salt-free content digest; a record edit, deletion, or non-v2 line injection is detected offline against a committed fixture.
The source tarball is deterministic and bound to the HEAD commit (reads git objects, not the working tree), so two builds from the same commit produce the same SHA-256 on any machine.
The release signing flow (cosign sign-blob → verify-blob over the reproducible tarball) runs offline with an ephemeral key as a dry-run; the real release uses the operator's long-lived key.

A deterministic planner decomposes a goal into specialist steps across typed JSON-Schema contracts, emitting a trust receipt per handoff into the HMAC audit chain; a golden trace replays it and the receipts are chain-verified + anchorable.
Every AI Act / GDPR article in the compliance matrix cites an artefact that exists; a deleted or renamed evidence file breaks the build, and the matrix cannot drift from INDEX.md.
A CycloneDX SBOM, cosign public key, and sigstore bundle ship for the release, asserted as hard requirements (no silent skips).

humanTrackItems.note: The seven personas are synthetic fixtures; code cannot produce real consented user sessions with measured outcomes.
Needs a paid third party; internal review + the prompt-injection/red-team harnesses are not an external audit.
Solo + one unnamed today; zero outside PRs. Code cannot manufacture a community.
Outreach drafts exist but are unsent; no signed partner.
Buildable proxy shipped: the in-repo reference agents pass the conformance suite. Genuine external adoption is a human-track outcome.
